question: In 2014 the 'Gangnam Style' video forced YouTube to change its view counter. Why?
answer: Its views were approaching 2,147,483,647, the largest number a 32-bit signed counter can hold. YouTube had never imagined a video passing it, so it moved to a 64-bit counter. Parker uses the case to show that computers store numbers in fixed sizes, and that limits which seem huge can be reached.
move: Every stored number has a limit; check it before it matters.
trap: 'Too many fake views': spam seems the likeliest trouble.
simply: YouTube's counter could only count to about 2.1 billion. When one video got close, they had to give it a much bigger counter.
why: The same kind of limit has caused real failures in planes, clocks and games. Asking 'what's the biggest number this can hold?' is a cheap check.
